series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$note: Trend: least-squares slope over 35 observed years (1990-2024) from DS-35, compared against the DS-06-NDC-LATEST target of 0.101 MtCO₂e by 2030. The two are not necessarily on the same inventory scope, see series.$note. The target tonnage is derived here, not quoted: 45% below DS-35's 2014 value of 0.184 MtCO₂e. The document states the percentage; the level it is applied to comes from DS-35, on DS-35's inventory scope, which is not necessarily the document's.
derived.$reason: observed emissions are rising by 0.00 MtCO₂e/yr while the target requires a fall of 0.02 MtCO₂e/yr. No multiple of the current trend reaches it, so no finite gap factor is reported.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "Dominica commits to progressively reduce total gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions below 2014 levels (164.5 Ggs est.) at the following reduction rates: 17.9% by 2020; 39.2% by 2025; and 44.7% by 2030...This contribution is conditional upon receiving timely access to international climate change financing, technology development and transfer, and capacity building support for priority adaptation and mitigation measures." Dominica has also outlined its plans for building climate resilience (adaptation), noting that "there is little distinction between adaptation and mitigation measures – an integrated response is being implemented to build climate resilience in vulnerable communities, while enabling Green Growth through the transition to sustainable energy technologies." See Dominica's INDC for more information.
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 17.9% by 2020, 39.2% by 2025 and 44.7% by 2030 reduction in GHG emissions below 2014 levels (164.5 Ggs est.)
ndc_assessment.sectors: Energy industries; Transport; Manufacturing and construction; Commercial/institutional, residential, agriculture, forestry, fishing; Solid waste
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

verdict.text: Dominica pledges a 45% reduction by 2030 against 2014 baseline (condition not read). The registry's current submission for this Party is The Commonwealth of Dominica Updated National Determined Contribution, filed 2022-07-04. 65 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (19). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 0.4 MtCO₂e, DS-35 0.2 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. The target is not reached on the observed trend. Both figures are on DS-35's inventory: the document's percentage applied to DS-35's 2014 level, not the document's own. It submitted BTR1. 0 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 58.5 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 17.9% by 2020, 39.2% by 2025 and 44.7% by 2030 reduction in GHG emissions below 2014 levels (164.5 Ggs est.) It was classed conditional. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +0.9°C under SSP1-2.6 to +2.99°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
